newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asian export banks seek closer regional ties.
newsitem.headline: Asian export banks seek closer regional ties.

text.p: Officials from export-financing institutions from seven Asian nations, meeting in Tokyo on Monday, agreed to seek closer cooperation in order to promote intra-regional commerce, Japan's Export-Import Bank said.

The meeting, hosted by the Ex-Im Bank of Japan, was attended by officials from the Export Finance and Insurance Corporation (EFIC) of Australia, the Export-Import Bank of China, the Export-Import Bank of India, the Export-Import Bank of Korea, the Export-Import Bank of Malaysia, the Export-Import Bank of Thailand as well as Japanese business executives.

The participants agreed to hold the meetings on an annual basis to strive for greater operational collaboration, including the selection of co-financing projects, and to exchange information on specific matters such as financing techniques, it said.
"This should greatly enhance operational cooperation and coordination among export financing institutions," Japan's Ex-Im bank said in a statement.
The officials discussed ways to promote cooperation between Japanese firms and Asian export-financing institutions, with a view to promoting intra-regional economic transactions, it said.
They also exchanged views and information on their respective project-financing operations to deal with possible increases of private infrastructure projects in Asian nations.
Asian economies have showed remarkable growth in recent years and are becoming the engine of world economic growth, the statement said.

The average economic growth rate in Asia was eight percent between 1989 and 1995 and the average rate of growth in exports was 15.3 percent. This compared to 2.7 percent and 7.2 percent, respectively, on a global basis in the same period, the statement said.
